---
title: "Quiz: the structure tensor"
---

Short questions to test your understanding. Try each on paper first, then open the answer. Eigenvalues of $J$: $\mu_1 \ge \mu_2 \ge 0$.

---

**Q1.** Why does averaging the gradient vectors in a window fail to find the orientation of a bright line?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Which way do the gradients point on the two sides of the line?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
On both sides the gradient points towards the line (towards the brighter middle): on one side in direction $\mathbf g$, on the other in $-\mathbf g$. They cancel, and the average is about zero although the orientation is perfectly clear. The outer product $\mathbf g\mathbf g^\top$ is the same for $\mathbf g$ and $-\mathbf g$, so averaging it does not cancel.
:::

---

**Q2.** The structure tensor has two scales, σ and ρ. What does each control?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
One is applied before the products, one after.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
σ is the scale of the gradient (the derivative of a Gaussian): it controls noise and which structures produce gradients at all. ρ is the width of the Gaussian window that averages the products: it controls how large a region is summarised by one tensor. Too small a ρ gives noisy orientations; too large a ρ blurs boundaries between differently oriented regions.
:::

---

**Q3.** Classify the window: (a) $\mu_1 = 900$, $\mu_2 = 5$; (b) $\mu_1 = 600$, $\mu_2 = 450$; (c) $\mu_1 = 2$, $\mu_2 = 1$ (noise gives up to about 10).

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
How many large eigenvalues?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(a) An edge or oriented texture (one large eigenvalue, coherence $(895/905)^2 = 0.98$). (b) A corner (or an isotropic, busy texture): two large eigenvalues, coherence $(150/1050)^2 = 0.02$. (c) Flat: both within the noise.
:::

---

**Q4.** The structure tensor is "the covariance matrix of the gradients". Describe the gradient point cloud of an edge, a corner and a flat region.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Plot every gradient in the window as a point $(L_x, L_y)$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Edge: the points lie along a line through the origin (all gradients parallel or antiparallel): a long thin ellipse. Corner: points along two different directions: a broad, roundish ellipse. Flat: all points near the origin: a tiny ellipse. The eigenvalues of $J$ are the squared half-axes of the ellipse (up to a factor).
:::

---

**Q5.** What is the Harris response $\det J - k(\operatorname{tr}J)^2$ (with $k = 0.05$) for $J = \begin{pmatrix} 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 8\end{pmatrix}$ and for $J = \begin{pmatrix} 16 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{pmatrix}$? Which is the corner?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Both have the same trace.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
First: $64 - 0.05 \cdot 256 = 51.2$, a corner. Second: $0 - 0.05 \cdot 256 = -12.8$, an edge (negative). Same trace (total gradient energy), but only the first has it in two directions.
:::

---

**Q6.** Why are there no corners at all if the window is switched off (ρ = 0)?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What is the rank of $\mathbf g\mathbf g^\top$?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Without averaging, $J = \nabla L\,\nabla L^\top$ at each pixel has rank 1: $\mu_2 = 0$ and $\det J = 0$. A single gradient has a single direction; two directions can only come from different pixels in a window. Every pixel looks like an edge, and the Harris response is never positive.
:::

---

**Q7.** Hessian or structure tensor? (a) Find the centre line of a blood vessel. (b) Measure the dominant fibre direction in a patch of collagen. (c) Find points to track between two video frames.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Second derivatives, signed, at centres; or squared first derivatives, unsigned, in windows?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(a) Hessian: the vessel's centre is where the curvature across it is strongest (the gradient is zero there). (b) Structure tensor: orientation and coherence of a texture in a window. (c) Structure tensor: corners (Harris or $\mu_2$), which can be found again after a shift.
:::

---

**Q8.** *(math)* Show that $\mathbf u^\top J\mathbf u$ is the average of $(\nabla L\cdot\mathbf u)^2$ over the window, and explain why its maximum over unit vectors is $\mu_1$.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
$(\mathbf g\cdot\mathbf u)^2 = \mathbf u^\top\mathbf g\mathbf g^\top\mathbf u$; then the Rayleigh quotient.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$(\mathbf g\cdot\mathbf u)^2 = (\mathbf u^\top\mathbf g)(\mathbf g^\top\mathbf u) = \mathbf u^\top(\mathbf g\mathbf g^\top)\mathbf u$; averaging is linear, so $\langle(\nabla L\cdot\mathbf u)^2\rangle = \mathbf u^\top\langle\nabla L\nabla L^\top\rangle\mathbf u = \mathbf u^\top J\mathbf u$. Writing $\mathbf u = \cos\phi\,\mathbf e_1 + \sin\phi\,\mathbf e_2$ in the orthonormal eigenvectors of $J$: $\mathbf u^\top J\mathbf u = \mu_1\cos^2\phi + \mu_2\sin^2\phi \le \mu_1$, with equality along $\mathbf e_1$.
:::
